text:
sam: kicking off preflight for 23:50 UTC change window. Targets: api v2.10.0, runtime 3.7.0, router 4.4.0, console 2.2.0. Window 23:50-02:20 UTC. Special: tenant-aware canary (tenant pinning) for high-value tenants + region-aware routing. Plan: tenant-only 1% for 10m -> global 5% 20m -> 25%. Rollback: immediate unpin of tenant maps and shift to router-stable. @ali (runtime), @meera (router), @ryan (console) ack blockers now.

ali: ack. Runtime 3.7.0 enables lazy-quant bundling and exposes LIVE_QUANT_HEADER. For tenant pinning we should keep LIVE_QUANT_HEADER suppressed to avoid per-tenant perf divergence; publishing variant runtime:3.7.0-quant-suppressed now.

meera: ack. Router 4.4.0 adds tenant-route priority and a region-steer policy. For tenant canary we'll apply ROUTER_TENANT_PIN=true and ROUTER_REGION_STEER=eu-only for initial wave. Also noticed new connection pool default increased to 200; I'll set POOL_MAX=150 for canary to match prod nodes.

ryan: console 2.2.0 will show tenant flags but the release toggle is behind org opt-in. I'll keep UI opt-in off until we confirm runtime + router are stable. SRE: watch p50/p95/p99, token latency, tenant error deltas. Abort if tenant 5xx >0.2% or global p99>820ms. Deploybot will enforce tenant routing mapping in the wave.

deploybot: queued wave #rw-17699. Canary config: {"tenant_pin_pct":1,"tenant_list":["tenant-a","tenant-b"],"stages":[{"pct":1,"mins":10},{"pct":5,"mins":20}],"abort_conds":["tenant_5xx>0.2%","global_p99>820ms"]}

sam: OK. Ali please ensure runtime variant tag is reachable from deploy pools and deploybot targets runtime-canary pool. Meera coordinate router env overrides.

meera: planned kubectl command for env overrides (canary namespace):
```
kubectl set env deploy/router-canary ROUTER_TENANT_PIN=true ROUTER_REGION_STEER=eu POOL_MAX=150 -n prod-canary
```

ali: runtime tag published: runtime:3.7.0-quant-suppressed. Please target runtime-canary pool.

deploybot: canary start triggered at 23:51 UTC. Sequence: runtime -> api -> router. Tenant pin applied for tenant-a,b at 1%. Rolling now.

deploybot: 1% tenant canary reached at 00:03 UTC. Shortchecks: tenant-a 200/200, tenant-b 199/200. Watching per-tenant metrics.

sre-bot: initial snapshot: global p99 700ms, tenant-a p99 880ms (higher), tenant-b p99 720ms. tenant-a shows increased token generation latency. Trace sample points to increased quantization CPU on runtime-12 pod for tenant-a traffic.

ali: I see the same on runtime logs: quant bundle warmup for model X triggers a CPU spike on pod runtime-12 when processing tenant-a requests. Snippet:
```
[00:04:12] INFO quant_bundle_warmup model=X duration=420ms pod=runtime-12
```
We suppressed LIVE_QUANT_HEADER but lazy bundling still warms on first tenant workload. Suggest pause and either prewarm bundles or rollback runtime to 3.6.4 for tenant canary subset.

sam: hold ramp. Pause router ramp. Ali, can you trigger a targeted runtime rollback for the affected tenant subset? If prewarm is quick we might prefer to prewarm now and resume without rollback.

ali: attempting live prewarm on affected canary pods via exec job to prebundle model X. Command:
```
kubectl exec job/prewarm-quant -n prod-canary -- ./prewarm --model X --pods runtime-12,runtime-13
```
Triggering now.

deploybot: prewarm job started and reported success at 00:09 UTC. Monitoring impact.

sre-bot: post-prewarm tenant-a p99 dropped from 880ms -> 730ms within 60s. Error rate unchanged. Global p99 back to 710ms.

sam: good mitigation. Resume canary to 5% global stage? Any objections?

meera: router is still at REGION_STEER=eu for tenant pin; that’s fine. I'll keep POOL_MAX=150. No objections.

ryan: console toggle remains off. No UI exposure yet.

deploybot: ramping to 5% global at 00:15 UTC. Monitoring per-tenant and region metrics.

sre-bot: at 00:28 UTC checks: global p95/p99 within baseline, tenant deltas normalized, 5xx stable. No infra anomalies. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/d/ops/release-watch?var=wave=rw-17699

sam: action items after window: 1) add a prewarm step to tenant-aware canary flows for heavy models, 2) ensure deploybot can trigger targeted prewarm jobs when runtime variant includes lazy-bundles, 3) add pool-level CPU headroom check before applying lazy quant on tenant-heavy pods. I'll file tickets and adjust release notes. Great quick mitigation.
ali: filing prewarm automation PR.
meera: adding router-POOL_MAX note to rollout docs.
ryan: will coordinate console opt-in timeline after we validate canary across regions.
sam: closing this preflight. We'll schedule a full window next week for gradual rollout across tenants and regions. Thanks everyone. :clap:
